24 terms

The words on the paperwork

Every term you are likely to meet at a counter or on a certificate, with the characters, the pinyin, and what it actually decides.

Property in China is discussed in a vocabulary that carries legal weight and is almost never translated in the room. Knowing the four characters on a certificate is the difference between understanding what you own and being told what you own.

The pinyin is included because you will hear these words spoken long before you see them written. Say the term out loud once; it is the fastest way to stop a conversation that has moved past you.

BCDFILMOPRSTV

B

  • 尾款

    wěi kuǎn

    Balance payment

    The remainder released when ownership transfers, normally held in escrow until the new certificate is issued.

    Where this matters: Escrow and payment stages: how not to lose a depositThe purchase timeline, week by weekMoving money into China for a property purchase

  • 毛坯 / 精装

    máo pī / jīng zhuāng

    Bare shell / fitted out

    Bare shell means no flooring, kitchen or bathroom — the common state of new builds. Fitted out means a specification you should read line by line, because it moves.

    Where this matters: Off-plan or resale? Two very different risk profilesNew build or resale — the taxes and fees are not the same

C

  • 商住

    shāng zhù

    Commercial-residential

    40- or 50-year units sold as apartments. Commercial utilities, no school catchment, higher taxes, shorter mortgages — and generally closed to foreign individual buyers.

    Where this matters: 70, 50 or 40 years: what the land term really means

  • 查封

    chá fēng

    Court seal

    A legal freeze on a property, usually from litigation or debt. A sealed unit cannot transfer. This is what a registry search is looking for.

    Where this matters: The due-diligence checklistMarriage, divorce and inheritance: who else has a claim on the flat

D

  • 契税

    qì shuì

    Deed tax

    The main tax a buyer pays at registration: 1% up to 140m² for a first or second home, 1.5–2% above, 3% for commercial stock or a third home.

    Where this matters: The full cost of buying: the 3–6% nobody budgets forThe purchase timeline, week by weekNew build or resale — the taxes and fees are not the same

  • 定金

    dìng jīn

    Deposit

    A commitment payment, usually 1–5% of price, against a written deposit agreement. Its refund conditions decide who carries the risk.

    Where this matters: Escrow and payment stages: how not to lose a depositThe purchase timeline, week by weekMoving money into China for a property purchase

  • 首付

    shǒu fù

    Down payment

    The buyer's equity contribution, paid into escrow after contract registration. For foreign buyers, typically 40–50% of price because loan-to-value is capped lower.

    Where this matters: Mortgages for foreign buyers: who lends, and on what termsThe purchase timeline, week by weekMoving money into China for a property purchase

F

  • 满五唯一

    mǎn wǔ wéi yī

    Five years, only home

    The condition that exempts a seller from individual income tax: held five years or more and the seller's only residential property. A standard negotiation term.

    Where this matters: The full cost of buying: the 3–6% nobody budgets forNew build or resale — the taxes and fees are not the sameMarriage, divorce and inheritance: who else has a claim on the flat

I

  • 个人所得税

    gè rén suǒ dé shuì

    Individual income tax

    On sale, typically 1% of price or 20% of the gain. Exempt where the property has been the seller's only home for five years or more.

    Where this matters: The full cost of buying: the 3–6% nobody budgets forSelling, and getting the money outNew build or resale — the taxes and fees are not the same

L

  • 土地使用权

    tǔ dì shǐ yòng quán

    Land-use right

    What you actually acquire over state-owned land, for a fixed term: 70 years residential, 50 institutional, 40 commercial. The clock starts at the land grant, not at your purchase.

    Where this matters: 70, 50 or 40 years: what the land term really means

  • LPR

    L P R

    Loan prime rate

    The benchmark rate Chinese mortgages are priced against, with a spread, and repriced annually. Compare total cost, not the headline rate.

    Where this matters: Mortgages for foreign buyers: who lends, and on what terms

M

  • 维修基金

    wéi xiū jī jīn

    Maintenance fund

    A one-off contribution at purchase, around 2–3% of price on new homes, held for major building repairs. Not a fee you can recover on sale.

    Where this matters: Property tax: what is actually in force, and whereNew build or resale — the taxes and fees are not the same

  • 抵押

    dǐ yā

    Mortgage / encumbrance

    A registered charge over the property, normally a bank loan. It must be discharged before transfer; a promise to release it later is not the same thing.

    Where this matters: The due-diligence checklistMarriage, divorce and inheritance: who else has a claim on the flat

O

  • 网签

    wǎng qiān

    Online contract registration

    The step that enters the sale into the housing authority's system, locking the unit against a second sale and formally testing your eligibility.

    Where this matters: Escrow and payment stages: how not to lose a depositCan foreigners buy property in China? The rules, city by cityThe purchase timeline, week by week

P

  • 预售许可证

    yù shòu xǔ kě zhèng

    Pre-sale permit

    The permission a developer needs before selling unbuilt units. It is building- and stage-specific; paying without one leaves your money unprotected.

    Where this matters: Off-plan or resale? Two very different risk profilesNew build or resale — the taxes and fees are not the same

  • 物业费

    wù yè fèi

    Property management fee

    Charged per square metre per month, roughly ¥3–15. On 120m² at ¥8 that is ¥11,520 a year — a sixth of the rent on a 1.7% yield.

    Where this matters: The full cost of buying: the 3–6% nobody budgets forProperty tax: what is actually in force, and where

  • 不动产权证

    bú dòng chǎn quán zhèng

    Property ownership certificate

    The single certificate that records who owns a building and the land-use right beneath it. It replaced the old 房产证 and 土地证 pair. Read four fields: nature of right, use, term end date, registered area.

    Where this matters: 70, 50 or 40 years: what the land term really meansCan foreigners buy property in China? The rules, city by cityThe purchase timeline, week by weekMarriage, divorce and inheritance: who else has a claim on the flat

  • 限购

    xiàn gòu

    Purchase restriction

    Municipal limits on who may buy and how many. For foreign nationals the effective limit is one self-use home, in the city of employment, after a qualifying year.

    Where this matters: Can foreigners buy property in China? The rules, city by cityThe one-year rule, and how it is actually verified

R

  • 住宿登记

    zhù sù dēng jì

    Residence registration

    The police-station registration a foreign national must complete after moving in, and after any address change. Hotels do it for you; private leases do not.

    Where this matters: Renting in China as a foreigner: contracts, deposits and registration

S

  • 学区

    xué qū

    School catchment

    The administrative mapping of address to school place. It drives large price premiums and is repriced by policy, not by the market.

    Where this matters: Choosing where to live in a Chinese city

  • 公摊面积

    gōng tān miàn jī

    Shared floor area

    The portion of the registered area allocated to corridors, lifts and common space, commonly 20–30%. It is why a 100m² unit may feel like 75m².

    Where this matters: 70, 50 or 40 years: what the land term really meansNew build or resale — the taxes and fees are not the same

  • 资金监管

    zī jīn jiān guǎn

    Supervised escrow

    An account held jointly by buyer, seller and bank, released only when named documents are produced. The mechanism that stops a deposit disappearing with a seller.

    Where this matters: Escrow and payment stages: how not to lose a depositMoving money into China for a property purchase

T

  • 过户

    guò hù

    Transfer of ownership

    The registration step at which the property becomes yours. The balance in escrow is released against the new certificate, not against a promise.

    Where this matters: Escrow and payment stages: how not to lose a depositThe purchase timeline, week by weekMarriage, divorce and inheritance: who else has a claim on the flat

V

  • 增值税

    zēng zhí shuì

    Value-added tax

    Around 5.3% on resale, generally exempt where the seller has held the property for two years or more. Legally the seller's tax, often negotiated onto the buyer.

    Where this matters: The full cost of buying: the 3–6% nobody budgets forNew build or resale — the taxes and fees are not the same

If a term you met is missing, that is a gap worth reporting — tell us and it will be added with the same treatment.
